text:
kim: Quick thought — we've been iterating on the continuous-batcher, but I think we should discuss a refactor that surfaces richer backpressure signals from the queue into the admission layer. goal: avoid long-tail starvation without adding per-tenant timers.
arpit: +1. are you thinking about adding more metrics or changing the admission contract?
soraya: curious — what signals would be cheap enough to compute in hot path?
kim: mainly three small signals: queue-depth-by-size, inflight-kv-cache-pressure, and recent-eviction-rate. together they should guide soft-deprioritization before we preempt.
mike: eviction-rate is interesting. we saw spikes when gc/kv-evict runs hit big tenants. how do we avoid thrashing?
kim: idea: introduce a short-lived exponential decay counter (50–200ms half-life) for evictions per-tenant and a separate headroom score. admission uses both to raise a "soft-hold" flag that doesn't preempt immediately, just reduces batch eligibility.
soraya: sounds lightweight. implementation sketch? pseudo: ```
# enqueue path
tenant.eviction_score = tenant.eviction_score * decay + recent_evictions
if tenant.eviction_score > EVICT_THRESH: tenant.soft_hold = true
```
elaine: we should be careful about nested effects — soft_hold reduces batching which might increase tail latency and cause more evictions. need stability.
arpit: agree. add hysteresis and a minimum cool-down window. maybe apply soft_hold only if both eviction_score and kv_cache_pressure exceed thresholds.
mike: can we reuse existing reservation tokens as a place to carry the headroom hint? avoids changing the hot path shape too much.
kim: yes — reservation token already flows from admission to batcher. add a small enum: {NORMAL, SOFT_HELD, FORCED} and a byte for score. cheap to attach.
soraya: rollout plan? we need safe defaults and a way to opt-out per-tenant.
kim: phased rollout: 1) telemetry-only: emit candidate signals and show dashboards, no behavior change. 2) opt-in per team via config flag (dev and small set of tenants) 3) global opt-in with conservative thresholds 4) enable hysteresis tuning experiments.
telemetry-bot: kim configured telemetry stream: continuous-batcher.signals.{queue_depth,eviction_score,kv_pressure,soft_hold_count} -> datadog (low-card)
elaine: telemetry first is critical. can we tag metrics with fastpath/slowpath so we can see impact on small request latencies?
kim: yes, add path tag: path=fastpath|microbatch|bulk. also emit sample of batch sizes when soft_hold was applied.
arpit: what about SLO safety? we need a circuit breaker that disables soft-hold if tail P99 error rate rises.
soraya: propose: controller monitors p99_generation_latency and p99_error. if either increases >X% in 5m after rollout, auto-disable soft_hold for 10m and alert.
mike: testing: unit tests + an integration fuzz that replays production traces with and without soft_hold to measure throughput and tail. canary scenario should include a "runaway-tenant" trace.
kim: agree. also need to update rollout docs in the console: per-tenant toggle + suggested thresholds and when to fall back.
elaine: can we implement shadow-apply mode where soft_hold is computed but not applied, then we compare predicted decisions vs what actually happened?
arpit: yes, shadow mode is low-risk. add a small sampler to keep overhead minimal.
soraya: question on observability: we must avoid high-cardinality tags (tenant id) in primary metrics. use tenant bucketing (small/medium/large) and only annotate top n tenants in detailed logs.
kim: good call. runtime will emit low-card metrics, and we can stream detailed samples to a separate long-tail bucket for offline analysis.
mike: any API changes? none for customers, just internal config flags. but we should keep the migration path clear for Private deployments — docs and feature gates.
kim: next steps: i'll draft a short RFC with diagrams, config knobs, and the telemetry table. volunteers for review?
arpit: I'll take infra-level API + token bits.
soraya: I'll own telemetry and dashboards.
elaine: I'll write the rollout playbook and circuit-breaker thresholds.
mike: I'll add the integration harness and traces for fuzzing.
kim: awesome — I'll post the RFC by EOD tomorrow. thanks all :thumbsup:
